x: Shortly after this point he was overtaken by Len Bishop, the Club title holder, who was determined that his title would not be relinquished at any price.
(This is generally kept in the safe and only available to order). LEN'S THE TAMING OF A STEW A NEW DIMENSION TO GOOD LIVING AT COLEMAN'S CHOP HOUSE
Carl, John and Ray produced their usuals but Len was the real match winner in 6th place. John Bromley came in together with Munich Olympian Howard Timms.

I am not sure about the date of the photograph on page 63 but it is Joe Coleman, not Len, wearing number 7. I do not recall him walking much after I joined the Club in October 1948 and I suspect that it was taken around that year.
This was followed by 3rd in the Southern and 6th in the National with the lead man on each occasion being Jack Brown with Charlie Walker, Len and Alan Bishop, along with Dennis Brickwood in the team.
He was contemporary with Arthur Penny, Bert Footer, Vic Blowfield, Ted Stimpson, Charlie Smart, Harry Shields, Len Marchant, Bill Lucas, my brother Len and many others.
